ai.description: *Cnemaspis shevaroyensis* is a small gecko (SVL ~35 mm) with a brown dorsum featuring yellow-spotted longitudinal rows. It is distinguished by a prominent precloacal pore and a lack of keeled ventral scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis shevaroyensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous yellow or white vertebral stripe that extends from the nape to the tail base.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis shevaroyensis* inhabits rocky crevices and boulders within moist deciduous forests of the Shevaroy Hills, typically at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Cnemaspis shevaroyensis* is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small insects on rocky surfaces and tree trunks during the sunlit hours of the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis shevaroyensis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, with peak activity during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis shevaroyensis* is endemic to the Shevaroy Hills in the Eastern Ghats of Tamil Nadu, India, typically occurring at elevations between 1,200 and 1,500 meters.
